subject: Post-demo: Novasecure integration — routing, auth, and fallback implementation checklist
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Novasecure integration — routing, auth, and fallback implementation checklist

Thanks again for the time earlier, Daniel — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed implementation checklist based on the architecture conversation: 

1) Sandbox + SDK access
   - We will provision a scoped sandbox project for Novasecure with a dedicated API key and example SDK snippets (Python/Node).
   - Action: Redwood (Ben) to create sandbox and share credentials; Novasecure to validate connectivity.

2) Auth and IAM
   - Recommend TLS + per-service API keys for the initial integration. For production, we support KMS-backed keys and VPC private link if you want full network isolation.
   - Action: Novasecure to confirm preference (API key vs KMS).

3) Routing & model policy
   - Primary model: open-xlarge (cost-optimized for bulk embeddings/requests).
   - Latency-critical routing: route user-facing chat through low-latency pool (region us-west) with strict 95th pct latency SLO.
   - Fallback chain: low-cost -> standard -> high-accuracy models. Automatic failover if the chosen pool reports sustained queueing > 200ms.
   - SDK-level hinting: user_request.metadata.routing_hint can be set to prefer cost or latency.

4) Structured output & tool calling
   - We recommend using Redwood's structured-output schema v1 for tool calls; we'll provide examples for your reranker + external search connector.

5) Embeddings & reranker flow
   - Batch embeddings in nightly jobs for full dataset; use real-time incremental embedding for user content.
   - Reranker sits after retrieval: retrieval -> embedding similarity -> reranker model to reorder top-K.

Attachments: redwood-routing-playbook-v1.md (playbook draft), sample SDK snippets.

Proposed next steps:
- I will create the sandbox and drop a README + SDK examples into the sandbox project by EOD tomorrow.
- Marcus to produce a short routing policy matrix (latency/cost/tradeoffs) and share for review.
- Please send the security questionnaire when you have it; Monica will take point on the responses.

If that looks right, can we schedule a 30-minute ops tech call next Tue (27th) to confirm routing SLOs and failover thresholds?

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Daniel — quick responses inline: 

- Sandbox IP restriction: yes — we can bind API keys to IP ranges. We'll provision a key restricted to your VPN CIDR and rotate it on request.

- KV cache & session state during fallback: by default, KV cache is tied to a session token stored by the SDK. If we route a request to a different model pool in the same region, we preserve KV if using the same session id and compatible model family. Cross-region fallbacks will not preserve GPU-side KV; in that case we provide client-side warmup tokens to reduce cold-step latency. We recommend configuring the fallback policy to prefer same-region pools for chat sessions where KV preservation is required.

- Reranker cost: rough estimate for a typical top-10 rerank (reranker model + retrieval scoring) is ~0.8x the cost of a standard generation call per user request; depends on model choice and token footprint. We'll run a quick cost sim against your sample workload once we have token distributions.

Routing policy matrix (summary):
- Latency-critical (SLO 200ms 95th): route to low-latency pool in us-west; reserve 2x headroom autoscale.
- Cost-sensitive (batch/embeddings): use quantized CPU/GPU pool, asynchronous batching.
- Graceful degradation: if queue depth causes >200ms queuing for 30s, auto-fail to next model in chain.

I'll upload a short matrix and the fallback-as-code snippets to the sandbox project. Ben — I'll need access to the HubSpot deal ID to tag the sandbox. Monica — I'll take the security questionnaire and begin answers; will flag any items requiring legal.

-Marcus
